title: AOM Site Redesign Visual Audit
summary: Visual audit of AOM site redesign across iPhone SE, iPhone 12 Pro, and Desktop.
content:
AOM Site Redesign Visual Audit

URL: https://aheadofmarket.com Date: 2026-03-08 Viewports tested: iPhone SE (375x667), iPhone 12 Pro (390x844), Desktop (1440x900) Pages: Homepage (/), Brand (/brand)

Overall Verdict

The redesign is strong. The new sections are all present and well-structured. The warm palette lands. Typography is bold and confident. A few mobile issues worth addressing before calling it done.

Homepage

Hero

  • Status: Looks right across all viewports
  • Title reads "BRAND INFRASTRUCTURE FOR COMPANIES THAT BUILD." with "BUILD" in orange italic
  • Subtitle text is readable and well-spaced
  • Desktop: CTAs ("SEE WHAT WE'D BUILD FOR YOU" and "SEE THE WORK") are visible below the fold
  • Mobile: CTAs visible on iPhone 12 Pro but clipped on iPhone SE (shorter viewport cuts them off)
  • "CREATIVE PRODUCTION + SYSTEMS" label is present above the headline

Services Grid ("Three Ways In")

  • Status: Present and working
  • Desktop: Clean 3-column grid (Content Engine, Production, Digital Infrastructure)
  • Mobile: Stacks to single column correctly
  • Cards have icons, descriptions, and "Learn more" links
  • Good spacing and hierarchy

Construction Callout

  • Status: Present and effective
  • Headline: "YOUR COMPETITOR'S INSTAGRAM IS THEIR BEST RECRUITER. IS YOURS?"
  • Three pain points listed: Recruiting, Winning Bids, Looking Legitimate
  • Ambition Mechanical proof point with stats (30+ posts/month, 1 filming day)
  • Desktop: Side-by-side layout works well
  • Mobile: Stacks cleanly

AI Teaser ("The System Behind the Brand")

  • Status: Present
  • "We built an AI system that runs our own business. Now we're building them for clients."
  • Pipeline visualization: INPUT (1 filming day) > SYSTEM (content.pipeline.run()) > OUTPUT (30 days of social content)
  • Feature bullets visible
  • "WE BUILT THIS FOR OURSELVES FIRST" with early access email capture
  • Clean on both desktop and mobile

Phoenix Production / Social Proof

  • Stats displayed: 55+ (services/hospitality/STEAM), 31+ (regional reach), 87+ (assets shipped)
  • Three testimonials with names and companies (Brandon Clarke, Sumit Seth, Gio Osso)
  • Desktop: 3-column stat cards with testimonials below
  • Mobile: Stacks vertically, readable

Portfolio

  • Filter tabs: MARKETING, BUILDERS, FOUNDERS
  • Video thumbnail grid with project titles and tags
  • "SWIPE TO EXPLORE" indicator on mobile (good UX)
  • Desktop: Multi-column grid
  • Mobile: Horizontal swipe cards

Execution Path ("Choose Your Execution Path")

  • 6 service tiers with pricing:
    • The Big Launch: $10k-$25k
    • Content Engine: $3k/mo
    • Founder Authority: $5k+
    • Social Proof: $5k+
    • Event Capture: $3k+
    • The Wildcard: Tailored
  • Desktop: 3x2 grid, scannable
  • Mobile: Single column stack, all readable

Why Us ("The Reason This Works")

  • 4 pillars: Tight Timelines, 24-72HR, Cinema-Grade, Repeatable
  • Desktop: Clean 4-column card layout
  • Mobile: Stacks to single column

Footer CTA

  • "READY TO SCALE?" with "START BRIEF" (orange) and "BOOK CALL" buttons
  • Contact info: Call Production, hello@aom-inhouse.com
  • Clean and punchy on desktop
  • Not captured on mobile scroll but heading structure confirms it's there

Brand Page (/brand)

Structure

  • Sections: AOM Brand Guidelines, Who We Are, Warm Not Cold (palette), Three Fonts Clear Roles, Look and Feel, Build With These, Portfolio, How We Talk
  • Desktop: Left sidebar nav with section links
  • Mobile: Stacks vertically, sidebar becomes inline

Visual Quality

  • Desktop: Very clean, well-organized brand guide layout
  • Mobile: All sections render correctly, content is readable
  • Color swatches visible in "Warm, Not Cold" section
  • Typography specimens displayed clearly
  • Page is long (16,045px on mobile, 11,663px on desktop) but appropriate for a brand guide

Palette Check

  • Background: rgb(2, 2, 2) -- very close to the target #0A0A08, reads as the same warm near-black
  • Text: Warm white throughout, not pure white
  • Orange accents: Present on CTAs ("GET STARTED", "START BRIEF", "SEE WHAT WE'D BUILD FOR YOU"), stat highlights, section labels, and the italic "BUILD" / "SCALE" / "PORTFOLIO" / "WORKS" words
  • Verdict: Warm palette is applied correctly

Issues Found

P1 (Fix before launch)

  1. iPhone SE hero CTAs clipped -- On the 375x667 viewport, the two CTA buttons below the hero subtitle are not visible without scrolling. The hero takes up the full screen. Consider reducing hero min-height on very small screens or making the CTAs more prominent.

  2. Sticky nav overlaps content on scroll -- The fixed "AOM." header + "GET STARTED" button overlaps content text at the top of several sections as you scroll through them. Visible on mobile sections 7, 8, 11, 12, 13, 14 where text runs behind/under the nav bar. Add scroll padding or top margin to sections.

P2 (Should fix)

  1. "FOUNDERS" tab label truncated on mobile -- In the portfolio filter tabs, "FOUNDERS" is cut off to "FOUNI..." on iPhone 12 Pro (390px). The tabs need to either scroll horizontally with visible overflow or use shorter labels on mobile.

  2. Small touch targets -- 9-10 elements on mobile and 28-34 on the brand page fall below the 44x44px minimum recommended touch target size. Most are likely nav links and small "Learn more" arrows. Worth auditing the most common interactive elements.

  3. Brand page has more small touch targets than homepage -- 28 of 36 interactive elements on mobile brand page are undersized. The sidebar nav links on desktop (which become inline on mobile) are likely the culprit.

P3 (Nice to have)

  1. Full-page screenshot not possible -- The <main> element uses h-screen overflow-y-auto as a scroll container instead of native body scroll. This means Playwright's fullPage: true only captures the viewport, not the full content. Not a user-facing issue, but worth noting if you ever need full-page OG images or print stylesheets.

  2. Portfolio section on mobile -- The horizontal swipe cards work, but some video thumbnails have overlaid text that's small. Not a blocker but could be more readable.
